text: First, he hurt the love of his life.
Then he spent
the rest of his life protecting her son.
At eleven, Severus Snape went to Hogwarts,
a hidden school of magic.
Inside, a magic hat places students
in rival houses:
Gryffindor for the brave, Slytherin for the ambitious.
As a lonely boy, he'd met Lily,
a girl from a non-magical family
who made flowers bloom.
Lily became a Gryffindor, Severus a Slytherin.
They stayed friends,
but he drifted toward dark magic.
James Potter, a Gryffindor bully, humiliated him.
Lily defended him.
Some wizards despised children of non-magical parents,
and had a slur for them.
To prove he didn't need her,
he called her that word.
Mudblood.
She never forgave him.
She married James.
Severus joined Voldemort,
the most feared dark wizard alive.
He passed his master a prophecy,
then realized it meant Lily's baby son.
He begged Dumbledore, the headmaster, to hide her.
It wasn't enough.
So he promised
to protect the boy with her eyes.
But Harry had her eyes in James's face,
so he guarded him and tormented him.
That explains it.
It doesn't excuse it.
Asked if he cared for the boy,
he conjured a silver doe,
a memory of Lily.
After all this time?
Always.
Dying, he asked Harry for one last thing.
Look at me.
Maybe so the last thing
he ever saw was her eyes.
